_comment: delegation/ORCHESTRATION.json — the run config for an autonomous build (D32). Copy into the consumer project's delegation/ folder and fill in. Read by scripts/orchestrate.mjs; also read by an auditor spawning workers natively. See prompts/AUTONOMOUS-BUILD.md Step 3.
_harness: claude-code | codex | generic. Selects which workerCmd preset applies. Purely descriptive if your harness spawns subagents natively.
_workerCmd: The command that starts ONE worker session, as a shell command line. {{TASK_ID}} and {{PROMPT_FILE}} are substituted. Leave empty if your harness spawns subagents natively — then orchestrate.mjs is not used at all. Copy one of the shapes from _workerCmdPresets below and CONFIRM IT against that CLI's own --help before the first wave: flags move, and a stale preset fails identically for every task, at 3am, three times over. Run one worker by hand on one task first.

_workerCmdPresets._note: Verified 2026-08-26 against each tool's own headless/non-interactive documentation. All three also accept a prompt on stdin and exit 0 on success, which is what orchestrate.mjs reads. Re-check before relying on them — this is exactly the kind of claim SPEC-AUTHOR.md's B-pass (check for rot) exists to catch.

_remoteWorkers: For execution mode `auditor-remote` (D35) the auditor runs here and the workers run on another provider's CLI. Watch for capability asymmetry: a weaker worker model needs a tighter brief and a narrower task, and it fails subtly and confidently rather than loudly. For a genuinely hard task — a from-scratch algorithm, a security-sensitive path, a concurrency question — put that one on a frontier model at extended/max thinking.
_maxParallel: How many workers run at once. Start at 2-3. More contention than you expect comes from the gate, not the code.
_maxRetries: How many times a failing task is re-issued to a FRESH worker before it is marked failed. The auditor never patches worker output itself — that would make it both author and reviewer.
_tierPolicy: Which escalation tiers a worker may decide alone. T2 always stops and asks. Uncertainty resolves to T2, never T1 — see lib/patterns/tiered-escalation.md §1.2.
_haltOn: Conditions that stop the WHOLE run rather than parking one task. Keep this near-empty: a T2 parks its own task and its dependents, and everything else keeps building. Reasonable entries: 'gate-red-after-integration', 'repo-dirty-outside-task-scope'.
